name: opendune
title: OpenDUNE (Watcom / DOS4GW, video_dos)
_doc: A REIMPLEMENTATION, not an original release -- so running it says PRISM handles a large modern-C DOS program, not that it runs unmodified 1990s source the way Quake and Heretic do. Different claim, worth keeping straight. What makes it cheap is that the project ships Makefile.wc: Watcom, DOS4G, flat model, video_dos.c, and author-maintained dsp_none/midi_none/crashlog_none backends -- exactly the environment PRISM already has for Heretic and Hexen.
_units: Straight from Makefile.wc's object lists. Its p/sl/s/t filename prefixes are not reproduced: they exist only because Watcom's object directory is flat and src/, src/pool/ and src/saveload/ all contain house.c. PRISM's units carry their full path, so nothing collides.
_defines: Makefile.wc's coptions: /bt=DOS4G /dDOS /i=..\include. __GNUC__ is UNDEFINED for the same reason Quake undefines __i386__: PRISM's target macros claim gcc because the emitted code is gcc-shaped, and src/os/strings.h reads __GNUC__ as 'this is not Watcom' and hands out glibc prototypes with __THROW and __restrict in them. A Watcom build never sees that branch.
_inline: src/rev.c is generated from rev.c.in by findversion.sh, which substitutes !!VERSION!! and !!MODIFIED!!. This is that build step's output, and 1 is its own documented value for 'built from sources with no version control'.
_include: Makefile.wc passes /i=..\include and nothing else. Adding src/ as well looks harmless and is not: <string.h> then finds OpenDUNE's own src/string.h instead of the libc one. The makefile's .c search path is for SOURCES, not includes.
